scenario: AITA for catching my parents disputes on a video conference when I'm working from home? | I am in my early 20s and I have a full time job. I'm living at home right now because, right when cuarantine was starting, I tried to renew my apartment lease and my landlord refused me, saying he was selling the building for condos. So with all the shutdowns, I wasn't able to find a new apartment in time and my parents let me move back in. It's really not ideal and I've actually signed a new apartment lease that starts in a month. I wish it was sooner but housing near me is very competitive. My parents have always had a very disfunctional relationship. But they won't leave each other. No matter how much drama they have, I think they've lived like this too long to consider anything else. First, unfortunately, that kind of thing has been really normalized for me, it doesn't register as a big deal. I said that I wasn't trying to film them, I was on camera myself because I was doing a presentation and they walked right in and started screaming. I think I might to keep the peace but I don't really feel bad for what I did. AITA for getting my parents argument on a video conference?
